title: Enterprise Onboarding: Comprehensive Support, Escalation, Integration & QBR Playbook
author: Maya Patel
content:
Purpose

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended runbook for enterprise onboarding, integration handoffs, escalation procedures, known issues & workarounds, and recurring health check / QBR materials. It is intended for Customer Success (CS) managers, Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and SRE partners to run predictable, low-risk enterprise launches and ongoing account health activities.

Scope

- Applies to all enterprise customers ( Dedicated and Private deployments ) during the initial 90-day onboarding window and ongoing quarterly reviews.
- Covers: kickoff, technical integration, validation, go-live, post-go-live support, escalation tiers, known issues reference, and QBR agenda/metrics.

Key Definitions

- Onboarding Owner: CS manager responsible for program delivery and customer satisfaction.
- Technical Lead: SE assigned to integration, network, and model onboarding tasks.
- SLO: Service-level objective defined per account (see "SLA & Targeting" section).

Roles & Responsibilities

- Customer Success (owner): Executive touchpoints, QBRs, milestone tracking, ROI/usage guidance.
- Solutions Engineering (owner): API integration, model selection, test harnesses, performance validation.
- Support (owner): Ticket handling, tiered escalations, incident routing.
- Eng-SRE (support): Capacity planning, production incident response, root cause analysis (RCA).
- Customer: Provide network access, test data, personas and acceptance criteria.

Pre-Onboarding Checklist (to complete before Kickoff)

1. Contract & Access
   - Confirm account type (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and contract terms (committed throughput, retention, SLAs).
   - Provision account in Redwood Console and create initial API key with scoped permissions.

2. Security & Network
   - For Private / VPC: validate connectivity (VPN or Direct Connect), firewall rules to redwood-api, outbound ports 443.
   - For Dedicated: confirm peering and IP allowlist entries.

3. Data & Compliance
   - Customer to confirm data residency and KMS requirements.
   - Exchange minimal test set (5-10 canonical prompts) and any PII redaction requirements.

Kickoff (Week 0)

- Attendees: CS owner, Technical Lead, Customer PM, Customer Engineers, Support rep (optional), SRE liaison (as needed).
- Agenda: scope, success criteria, go-live date, ops contacts, security review, rollout plan, QBR cadence.
- Deliverables: Onboarding plan, acceptance tests, communication matrix, escalation contacts.

Integration Phase (Week 1-4)

Checklist items (technical):
- API connectivity: issue a scoped API key and validate using API health endpoint: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
- Model selection & profiling: recommended default model is rwd/base-1.1 for evaluation; capture token distribution and latency distribution using sample traffic.
- Rate limiting & quotas: confirm per-route quota with customer (example: 50 req/s steady, 200 req/s burst).
- Prefix caching: enable prefix cache for repeat prompt patterns; verify cache hit-rate using Console > Routes > Metrics.
- Observability: ensure customer has read access to per-route dashboards and synthetic checks.

Validation & Performance (Week 2-5)

- Run acceptance tests: functional correctness on canonical prompts, latency percentiles (p50 < 120ms, p95 < 450ms for Hosted; Dedicated targets documented in contract).
- Cost estimate: run 7-day sample workload to project per-token cost using Redwood Optimize recommendations.
- Failover tests: simulate model fallback and region failover; verify traffic routing and no-data leakage.

Go-Live (Week 4-8)

- Criteria to flip traffic: all acceptance tests passing, security sign-off, capacity verified, support rotation assigned.
- Cutover options: gradual ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with monitoring windows and rollback plan.
- Post-go-live validation: 24/72 hour hypercare with daily syncs.

Support & Ticketing Process

- Intake: All customer issues should be opened in Zendesk (or company standard ticketing) and tagged with customer account and product area.
- Triage: Support does first-touch triage within 1 business hour for P1, 4 hours for P2, 24 hours for P3.
- Ownership: Support owns until reproduced or escalated to SE/SRE.
- Communication: Use standardized status updates every 24 hours for ongoing tickets; CS owner to receive copies for priority customers.

Severity / SLA Matrix

- P1 (Critical): Production outage (no inference for >50% of users) or data breach. Response: 15 minutes, continuous updates, engage SRE/Eng. Target resolution: 4 hours or mitigation plan.
- P2 (Major): Degraded service (latency or increased error rates impacting functionality). Response: 1 hour. Target resolution: 24-72 hours.
- P3 (Minor): Non-critical issues, feature requests, integration questions. Response: 1 business day. Target resolution: 7-14 days.

Escalation Playbook (Step-by-step)

1. Support Triage (0-1h)
   - Reproduce and gather logs: request request-id, route-id, sample prompt, timestamps. Collect Console trace URL.
   - If reproducible and P1/P2, open internal escalation channel (Slack #support-escalations) and tag SRE oncall.

2. SE Involvement (1-4h)
   - SE validates configuration, rate limiting, model variants, quantization profile.
   - If network or account limits, SE coordinates with customer to adjust allowlists or quota.

3. SRE / Eng Oncall (as needed)
   - SRE performs live investigation, increases logging, and triggers mitigation (e.g., route traffic to backup shard, increase autoscale).
   - If code-level bug suspected, create an incident in the internal incident tracker with severity and RCA owner.

4. Executive Escalation (24-72h)
   - If service impact or SLA breach risk remains after mitigation, CS leader notifies VP-CS and VP-Eng; schedule executive summary with customer within 48 hours.

Contact Matrix (primary -> secondary):
- Customer Success: cs-mgr-<account>@redwood.ai -> cs-lead@redwood.ai
- Solutions Engineering: se-<account>@redwood.ai -> se-lead@redwood.ai
- Support Pager: pagerduty-support@redwood.ai -> oncall-sre@redwood.ai

Known Issues & Workarounds (living list)

1. Issue ID: KIW-2027-01 - Intermittent 5xx from model shard during high token bursts
   - Symptoms: spikes in 500 responses correlated with long multi-turn sessions.
   - Root cause (interim): KV cache eviction under heavy concurrent sessions on older kernels.
   - Workaround: Enable continuous batching with max_batch_size reduced to 64 and enforce per-session token cap of 1,500 tokens. Schedule kernel patch (tracked with ENG-4248).

2. Issue ID: KIW-2027-07 - On-prem installer fails when proxy returns 403 for telemetry
   - Symptoms: installer aborts at telemetry check step.
   - Workaround: pre-seed installer config with telemetry.enabled=false or provide benign telemetry endpoint; support will validate post-install.

3. Issue ID: KIW-2026-12 - Model quality regressions after quantization profile change
   - Symptoms: deterministic prompt responses show lower coherence on evaluation set after switching to int8.
   - Workaround: revert to previous quantization profile, run A/B eval against acceptance test set, file model-regression ticket for research triage.

Support Escalation Templates (examples to paste in ticket)

- Subject: [P1] <Account> inference outage - <short description>
- Body: 
  1) Impact: number of affected users / percentage of API calls failing
  2) Steps to reproduce: exact prompt, model, route-id, sample timestamps
  3) Console links: traces, route metrics, logs
  4) Recent changes: deployments, config updates, quantization/profile changes

Health Checks & QBR Materials

Regular health cadence:
- Week 1 post-go-live: daily sync (30m) for hypercare.
- Month 1-3: weekly check-ins then biweekly as stable.
- Quarterly (QBR): Executive review of adoption, reliability, cost, and roadmap.

QBR Metrics (minimum)
- Usage: tokens/day (7d avg), peak TPS, monthly active users.
- Reliability: error rate (5xx)/successful requests, p50/p95 latency, uptime percentage. Target: uptime >= 99.9% for Dedicated / Hosted SLA per contract.
- Cost & Efficiency: cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate, batch utilization.
- Quality: regression rate on evaluation prompt set, customer-reported quality incidents.

QBR Agenda (60 minutes)
1. Executive summary (5m)
2. Adoption & business outcomes (10m)
3. Reliability & incidents (10m)
4. Performance & cost optimization recommendations (10m)
5. Roadmap & feature asks (10m)
6. Action items & owners (10m)
7. Open discussion (5m)

QBR Templates & Deliverables
- Pre-read document with the metrics dashboard export and key incidents since last QBR.
- Action item tracker (owner, due date, status).
- Follow-up meeting scheduled within 14 days for open action items.

Operational Playbooks & Runbooks (links)

- Incident response runbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process
- Support routing & triage: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process
- Integration step-by-step: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding-integration-playbook-2026.json

Maintenance & Continuous Improvement

- Quarterly review of the playbook by CS, SE, and SRE to add new known-issues, update SLAs, and incorporate product changes.
- Postmortem learnings must be fed back into onboarding checklists and the technical validation test suite.

Appendix: Example acceptance test checklist

- Functional: 10 canonical prompts return expected JSON key structure and function/tool calls where applicable.
- Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 450ms for typical Hosted requests.
- Resilience: fallback model triggers under simulated capacity constraint and returns responses within degraded latency SLO.
- Security: verified allowlist, KMS integration working, audit logging enabled.

Document History

- 2026-11-15: Created by Maya Patel (initial consolidated playbook).
- 2027-03-10: Added known-issues section and escalation templates (reviewers: Jordan Miles).
- 2027-11-15: Revised QBR metrics and severity SLA matrix (this revision).

If you are executing an onboarding and need assistance, open a request in Zendesk with tag "enterprise-onboarding" and assign CS owner. For urgent P1s, use the Support Pager and Slack channel #support-escalations.
